entries.label: EMA Guidelines
entries.title: Questions and answers on the PIP compliance verification procedure at EMA, and on paediatric rewards
entries.description: Questions and answers on the PIP compliance verification procedure at EMA, and on paediatric rewards
entries.summary: EMA released Q&A clarifying the PIP compliance verification process and paediatric reward eligibility.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must understand the verification steps to ensure compliance and accurately claim paediatric rewards, affecting all product types.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Notice of Compliance (NOC) Data Extracts
entries.description: The data extract is a series of compressed ASCII text files of the Notice of Compliance (NOC) database.
entries.summary: Release of Notice of Compliance (NOC) database extracts in compressed ASCII text format.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs teams should access the new data extracts to track compliance status for their products.

entries.label: EMA News
entries.title: Clinical trial applications advice pilot becomes permanent
entries.description: The Accelerating Clinical Trials in the EU (ACT EU) advice pilot, which helps sponsors prepare clinical trial applications, will become a permanent initiative from January 2027…
entries.summary: The ACT EU advice pilot for preparing clinical trial applications becomes a permanent initiative from January 2027.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs teams must now consistently utilize the ACT EU guidance for clinical trial applications, as it will be an ongoing requirement rather than a pilot.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Product monograph brand safety updates
entries.description: Product monograph brand safety updates for Submissions cleared between 01-09-2026 and 30-09-2026
entries.summary: Brand safety criteria in product monographs have been updated for all submissions cleared between 01-09-2026 and 30-09-2026.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must review and apply the new brand safety requirements to ensure compliance for affected products.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Guide to reporting and providing information on drug shortages and discontinuations (GUI-0120)
entries.description: This document is intended to help market authorization holders comply with sections C.01.014.8 to C.01.014.91 of the Food and Drug Regulations
entries.summary: Provides guidance on reporting and providing information on drug shortages and discontinuations to meet specific sections of the Food and Drug Regulations.
entries.why_it_matters: Market authorization holders must follow these sections, so RA teams need to incorporate the reporting procedures into their compliance processes.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Guide to distributing drugs intended for the Canadian market for consumption or use outside Canada (GUI-0145)
entries.description: This document is intended to help drug establishment licence holders comply with sections C.01.014.94 to C.01.014.95 of the Food and Drug Regulations.
entries.summary: Provides guidance for drug establishment licence holders on distributing drugs intended for the Canadian market for consumption or use outside Canada.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must ensure compliance with sections C.01.014.94 to C.01.014.95 when exporting Canadian market drugs, affecting licence holders and requiring adherence to the new guidance.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Guide on the exceptional importation and sale of drugs in response to shortages and discontinuations (GUI-0148)
entries.description: This document will help drug establishment licence holders comply with sections C.10.004 to C.10.013 of the Food and Drug Regulations.
entries.summary: This guide outlines procedures for the exceptional importation and sale of drugs during shortages or discontinuations to comply with sections C.10.004 to C.10.013 of the Food and Drug Regulations.
entries.why_it_matters: Drug establishment licence holders must follow these procedures to ensure lawful importation and sale of drugs during shortages or discontinuations, impacting regulatory compliance and supply chain management.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Guide on extending expiration dates of marketed drugs in response to drug shortages (GUI-0500)
entries.description: This document will help market authorization holders and drug establishment licence holders understand how to comply with sections C.010.014 to C.10.021 of the Food and Drug Regulations
entries.summary: The guidance allows market authorization holders to extend the expiration dates of marketed drugs to address drug shortages.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs teams responsible for marketed drugs must adjust expiry dates and update documentation to remain compliant.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Register of Innovative Drugs
entries.description: A listing of drugs pursuant to sub-section C.08.004.1(9) of the Food and Drug Regulations.
entries.summary: A new register of innovative drugs is established pursuant to sub‑section C.08.004.1(9) of the Food and Drug Regulations.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must be aware of which drugs are listed as innovative to ensure compliance with regulatory obligations and reporting requirements.

entries.label: EMA Guidelines
entries.title: European Medicines Agency pre-authorisation procedural advice for users of the centralised procedure
entries.description: European Medicines Agency pre-authorisation procedural advice for users of the centralised procedure
entries.summary: The EMA provides procedural guidance for applicants using the centralised procedure.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams applying for centralised approval must review the new procedural advice to ensure their submission process aligns with EMA expectations.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Drug Product Database data extract [2026-10-05]
entries.description: The Drug Product Database (DPD) extract files contain complete product information for all approved, marketed and cancelled products, for human, veterinary, disinfectant and radiopharmaceutical use.
entries.summary: The Drug Product Database (DPD) now provides data extract files that include complete product information for all approved, marketed, and cancelled products across human, veterinary, disinfectant, and radiopharmaceutical categories.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must be aware that the updated DPD extracts contain comprehensive product data, which will affect data management, compliance checks, and documentation for all therapeutic areas.

entries.label: EMA Guidelines
entries.title: List of centrally authorised products with safety-related changes to the product information

entries.summary: List of centrally authorised products with safety-related changes to their product information.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must review and update their product information and labeling to reflect the safety changes for the affected centrally authorised products.

entries.label: EMA News
entries.title: Advice on ‘end-of-year’ submission dates for type I variations in 2026
entries.description: Marketing authorisation holders wishing to receive an outcome in 2026 should submit type IA annual updates, individual type IA and type IAIN variations, and super-groupings…
entries.summary: The update provides guidance on the preferred end‑of‑year submission dates for type I and type IA annual updates and variations for 2026.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams holding marketing authorisation should note the recommended deadlines to ensure timely submission and avoid late penalties.

entries.label: EMA News
entries.title: EMA Management Board: highlights of September 2026 meeting
entries.description: Mid-year report 2026 from the Executive DirectorEMA presented results and achievements of its operations for the first half of 2026 to the Management Board. Between January and…
entries.summary: The EMA Management Board reviewed and approved updated operational guidelines for the first half of 2026.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must familiarize themselves with the new guidelines to ensure compliance with EMA requirements during the current reporting period.

entries.label: EMA News
entries.title: Global regulators call for advancing alternatives to animal testing across the medicine lifecycle
entries.description: EMA has endorsed a joint statement from the International Coalition of Medicines Regulatory Authorities (ICMRA) calling on medicine developers, manufacturers, regulators and…
entries.summary: Global regulators, including EMA, endorse a joint statement urging the advancement of non‑animal testing alternatives across the entire medicine development cycle.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams involved in product development and regulatory submissions must be aware that regulators are increasingly encouraging non‑animal methods, which may influence future requirements and submission strategies.

entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs teams will need to prepare for future requirements that may mandate inclusion of women's data in clinical development and regulatory submissions.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Updated Register of Certificates of Supplementary Protection and Applications
entries.description: Listing of drugs pursuant to sub-section 120(1) of the Certificate of Supplementary Protection Regulations.
entries.summary: The register of certificates of supplementary protection and applications has been updated.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams need to review the updated entries to ensure correct supplementary protection certificates for their products.

entries.label: EMA Guidelines
entries.title: Member states contact points for review of national implementation of quick response (QR) codes of veterinary medicinal products authorised via the centralised (CP), mutual recognition (MRP), decentralised procedures (DCP) and national procedures
entries.description: Member states contact points for review of national implementation of quick response (QR) codes of veterinary medicinal products authorised via the centralised (CP), mutual recognition (MRP), decentralised procedures (DCP) and national procedures
entries.summary: Member states have designated contact points to review the national implementation of QR codes for veterinary medicinal products authorised via CP, MRP, DCP and national procedures.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams should be aware of these contact points to coordinate compliance and reporting activities related to QR code implementation.

entries.label: EMA Guidelines
entries.title: INS-GCP-1 procedure for coordinating good-clinical-practice inspections requested by the CHMP

entries.summary: The INS-GCP-1 procedure establishes a coordinated approach for CHMP‑requested GCP inspections.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must follow this new procedure when preparing for inspections requested by the CHMP.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Monthly update to the generic submissions under review list
entries.description: This is a list of certain generic drug submissions currently under review. The Generic Submissions Under Review list includes the medicinal ingredient(s) and therapeutic area. Downloadable Excel files are included.
entries.summary: The FDA has released an updated list of generic drug submissions currently under review.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must monitor the list to track review status of their submissions and identify any potential changes that could affect approval timelines.

entries.label: EMA Guidelines
entries.title: Substances considered as not falling within the scope of Regulation (EC) No. 470/2009, with regard to residues of veterinary medicinal products in foodstuffs of animal origin
entries.description: Substances considered as not falling within the scope of Regulation (EC) No. 470/2009, with regard to residues of veterinary medicinal products in foodstuffs of animal origin
entries.summary: Certain substances are now excluded from the scope of Regulation (EC) No. 470/2009 for residues of veterinary medicinal products in foodstuffs of animal origin.
entries.why_it_matters: Veterinary RA teams must recognize that these substances no longer require residue compliance under this regulation and adjust monitoring and documentation accordingly.

entries.summary: MHRA launched a new Regulatory Advice Service for medical devices in December 2025.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams developing medical devices can now meet directly with MHRA for guidance, affecting their regulatory planning and support processes.

entries.label: EMA Guidelines
entries.title: Pharmacovigilance-related regulatory recommendations for centrally authorised veterinary medicinal products during 2026
entries.description: Pharmacovigilance-related regulatory recommendations for centrally authorised veterinary medicinal products during 2026
entries.summary: The European Medicines Agency updated its pharmacovigilance recommendations for centrally authorised veterinary medicinal products for 2026.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory Affairs teams responsible for veterinary medicinal products must review and adapt their pharmacovigilance plans to comply with the new recommendations.

entries.label: EMA Guidelines
entries.title: Draft guideline on veterinary good pharmacovigilance practices (VGVP) Module: Signal Management - Revision 1

entries.summary: Revision 1 of the VGVP signal management module introduces updated procedures for detecting and evaluating safety signals in veterinary medicines.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams managing veterinary products must revise their signal management processes to comply with the new guidelines.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Compliance and enforcement policy for health products (POL-0001)
entries.description: This policy describes Health Canada's national compliance and enforcement approach for health products regulated under the Food and Drugs Act and its regulations.
entries.summary: Health Canada has introduced a new national compliance and enforcement policy for all health products regulated under the Food and Drugs Act and its regulations.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams across all product types must review and align their compliance procedures with the updated policy to ensure continued regulatory conformity.
